title: Card skimming and digital pickpocketing
body_md:
## Where your card details get copied without your knowledge

Skimming is the practice of copying a card's data without the cardholder noticing. The data is later either embossed onto clone cards (less common now) or sold for online card-not-present fraud (the dominant use today).

The environment matters more than the technique. Knowing where the risk is high lets you focus your attention.

### Physical skimming locations

- **Outdoor ATMs and standalone payment terminals.** Anywhere a machine is not actively supervised. Skimmer hardware fits over the card slot or PIN pad; pinhole cameras record PIN entry.
- **Gas-station pumps.** The most common physical-skimming target in North America. Internal skimmers behind the pump panel can run for months before detection.
- **Restaurants where the card leaves your sight.** A waiter takes the card to a back terminal. Out of view, the card can be photographed or swiped through a portable skimmer.
- **Hotels and rental-car desks.** Manual key-entry of card numbers into a system creates a paper or electronic trail an insider can copy.

### Digital skimming (online)

- **Magecart attacks.** Attackers compromise an e-commerce site's checkout JavaScript so the page also sends your card details to their server while submitting the order to the real merchant. The order succeeds; you have no way to know it happened. Operates on big-name brands too — British Airways, Ticketmaster, Newegg have all been hit.
- **Compromised browser extensions.** A browser extension with permission to read web pages can capture card data on any site.
- **Open Wi-Fi sniffers.** Less of a risk now because almost all checkouts are HTTPS, but still an attack surface for badly-built sites.

### Defensive practices

1. **Use a virtual card.** Most modern banks and several specialised services (Apple Card numbers, Privacy.com, Revolut, Wise) generate single-use or merchant-locked virtual numbers. Compromise of a virtual number can't be reused elsewhere.

2. **Use tap-to-pay over the card chip wherever possible.** Apple Pay / Google Pay tokenizes every transaction; the merchant never sees your real card number.

3. **Wiggle the card slot before inserting it.** Genuine slots are firmly attached. Skimmer overlays usually wiggle or peel.

4. **Cover the PIN pad with your other hand.** A pinhole camera can be tiny, but it can't see through your hand.

5. **Keep card alerts on.** Real-time SMS or push notifications for every transaction give you minutes (not days) to spot fraud and freeze the card.

6. **Review your statement.** Skimmed cards often get tested with $1 charges before bigger purchases. Catching the test means freezing before the big charge runs.

### After a skim — the first hour

- Freeze the card in your bank's app. *Don't wait* to call a hotline.
- File a fraud claim while the transaction is still fresh — most issuers cap your liability at $0 with prompt reporting.
- Request a new card with a new number.
- Check every recurring subscription tied to the old number; update each.

widget_config.question: Which combination of habits provides the *strongest* practical defence against both physical and digital card skimming?

choices.text: Memorize your card number so you never need to enter it physically.
choices.explanation: Doesn't address physical skimming (which captures the chip / mag-stripe data, not your typing) or digital Magecart (which captures whatever the page submits).

choices.text: Pay with Apple Pay or Google Pay where possible, use a virtual card for the rest, and enable real-time transaction alerts.
choices.explanation: Yes. Tap-to-pay tokenises so the merchant never sees the real number — defeats both skimmer hardware and Magecart-style JS. Virtual cards limit damage where tap isn't available. Alerts give you minutes to react. This trio covers the realistic attack surface.

choices.text: Only shop on websites you've never used before.
choices.explanation: The opposite of defensive. New, unknown stores are higher-risk than established ones.

choices.text: Avoid paying for things online entirely.
choices.explanation: Removes one attack surface but leaves you fully exposed to physical skimming. Combination of tap + virtual + alerts is more practical and more effective.
